copy_detection.method: a string is a verbatim third-party copy when it contains a contiguous 10-word run that also occurs in the canonical third-party corpus

foreign_statement_scan.method: the rights gate's own grant scanner, over this manifest: a document that grants a licence over a path the manifest does not release, or over a path it releases under a different licence, contradicts the manifest

licences.CC-BY-4.0: the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence: applies to the material the authors authored inside the released set. It grants no right over third-party material, wherever that material occurs.
licences.MIT: the MIT licence: applies to the authors' own code. It grants no right over third-party material, wherever that material occurs.

open_questions.current_handling: not released; the copied text is withheld and replaced by pointer, commit, line range, permalink and sha256
open_questions.question: May the quoted source text in derived/records.jsonl (424 records, 827 code_context entries carrying text) be redistributed at all?
open_questions.subject: 424 v1 records quote Solidity from repositories that declare no licence
open_questions.why_not_mechanically_resolvable: The upstream repositories declare no licence, so there is no term to read and no permission to point at. The absence of a licence is not a grant, and this project has not obtained permission from the protocol authors. Only a rights holder - or a lawyer asked to judge the applicable jurisdiction - can answer it.

open_questions.current_handling: not released; the test name, framework, file, recorded impact and the hash of the removed text are kept instead of the text
open_questions.question: May the submitted proof-of-concept tests be redistributed as quoted evidence?
open_questions.subject: Code4rena contestant proof-of-concept code
open_questions.why_not_mechanically_resolvable: The code belongs to the contest participants. The pipeline never received a licence or a permission to sublicense it; a few submissions carry their author's own SPDX identifier and most carry none, which is an absence of a term rather than a permission. The Code4rena contest terms, and the applicable law, have to be read by a human.

open_questions.current_handling: not released; the citations are reference-only and the harness files are recorded in experiments/*/harness/WITHHELD.json
open_questions.question: Does the Change Date in BUSL-1.1 convert these citations to an open licence, and does the project want to rely on it?
open_questions.subject: BUSL-1.1 and Commons Clause audited repositories (reNFT, BakerFi, Wildcat)
open_questions.why_not_mechanically_resolvable: The terms permit use but not redistribution until their Change Date. Whether a given snapshot falls before or after that date for each repository is a question about each upstream commit and about the project owner's intent, not something a script can decide.

open_questions.current_handling: not released; the mined passages are withheld and the pointers, page locators and report hashes are kept
open_questions.question: Is every transformation this pipeline applies to an Oak Security report a derivative work barred by No-Derivatives?
open_questions.subject: Oak Security reports carry a CC BY-ND 4.0 term
open_questions.why_not_mechanically_resolvable: CC BY-ND forbids distribution of derivatives. Whether a mined field, a projected record or a digest is a derivative is a legal question that turns on the term and the jurisdiction. The project therefore withholds the passages rather than argue the question, but the question is not thereby answered.

open_questions.current_handling: not released; the addresses are removed from the distribution view and the canonical layers are left untouched
open_questions.question: How may the named individuals' work addresses in the Halborn Security reports be handled?
open_questions.subject: personal contact data mined out of third-party reports
open_questions.why_not_mechanically_resolvable: The addresses are personal data of identifiable people who never consented to publication. Redaction is a data-protection decision, not a copyright one, and the project's own legal basis for processing them has to be confirmed by a human.

policy.licence_assignment_rule: MIT for the authors' own code under scripts/ and tests/, CC-BY-4.0 for every other released path, and no licence at all for a path that is not released
policy.released_set_rule: a tracked path that is not listed in `paths` with a released rights_status is not part of the released set; the release process ships exactly the released paths

published_artefact_set: the set of tracked paths this project licenses for redistribution. Every other tracked path is retained in the research tree, is not licensed here, and is not cleared for redistribution

rules.why: the rights-redacted distribution view: this project's own projection, pointer records and decision artefacts
the VLUN pipeline: the authors' own code, MIT
the VLUN test suite: the authors' own code, MIT
the record schemas: the authors' own work
project documentation: the authors' own writing
the V4 per-source licence decision record: the authors' own decision, and the canonical statement of what each upstream source declares
V3 research notes written by the authors
the independent audit's own scripts and reports
the annotation guidelines and instruments written by the authors
generated analysis reports: the authors' own measurements and conclusions
continuous-integration configuration: the authors' own work

attribution_required.definition: carries third-party short quotations or names third-party authors, so a reuser must attribute the original author. Attribution is not a redistribution right.

internal_research_artefact_not_cleared.definition: the project's own working artefact whose rights position is not established. It is retained in the research tree, it is not part of any published artefact, and it is not cleared for redistribution.

metadata_only.definition: factual metadata the project recorded: identifiers, severities, labels, commit and file pointers, hashes. METADATA_ONLY is a default data-handling policy, not a legal clearance; a hash and a URL identify bytes and grant nothing.

project_own.definition: written by the VLUN authors: their own code, documentation, schemas, decision records and analysis. MIT for the code under scripts/, CC BY 4.0 for the documents and data.

withheld_third_party_no_redistribution_r.definition: carries copied third-party expressive content - source text, proof-of-concept code, fixing diffs or mined report prose - for which no documented right to redistribute is on file. It is not part of the released set.
